ugc.title: What is a creator-style AI video ad?
paras: UGC means user-generated content. Here, a creator-style ad uses an AI-generated person and casual phone-video framing; it is not a real customer review or endorsement.

An [AI UGC video ad](page:video-ads) gives you that look without hiring a creator or shipping your product to anyone. You upload a photo of your product, pick a style or describe the scene, and AIVideosUGC makes a 6, 10, 15 or 30 second clip built around your real product.

The people in these clips are generated by AI, not real customers, so use them to show the product rather than as reviews. Captions, music and prices go on afterward in your editor or ad tool, where you control every word.

faq.q: What can I make with AIVideosUGC?
faq.a: Short video ads, product and unboxing videos, white-background photos, lifestyle photos, model photos and social ad images. Most start from a photo of your product.
A clear photo of the product you sell. A phone photo on a plain background works well. Only upload photos you own or have permission to use.

faq.q: Can I use a product page link to start a video?
faq.a: Yes. Use [URL to Video](/ai-video-generation/url-to-video) with your product page link to start a video generation.

faq.q: How many videos and photos do I get each month?
faq.a: A product photo or a 6-second video uses 24 credits, a 10-second video 40, a 15-second video 60 and a 30-second video 120. The Starter plan's 200 credits cover about eight photos or three 15-second videos a month.

faq.q: Is the person in the video a real creator?
faq.a: No. The people in AI UGC videos are generated by AI, so show the product with them rather than presenting the clip as a customer review. Some platforms ask you to label AI-generated content.

faq.q: Does AIVideosUGC add narration, music, or captions?
faq.a: No. AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions. Add them in TikTok, CapCut, or your usual editor after you download, and type prices or offers there so every word is right.

faq.q: Can I try it for free?
faq.a: Not right now. There's no free plan, and checkout isn't open yet — the pricing page lists the planned Starter, Pro and Premium offers. Every photo or video shows its credit cost before it's made.

faq.q: What should I make first for a new product?
faq.a: Start with a clear product image for the listing. Add a lifestyle or detail photo when shoppers need context, then use a video when movement helps show the product.

faq.q: Which video type should I make first?
faq.a: Choose an ad to introduce the product, a demo for one action, an unboxing to show the package reveal, or photo animation to add movement to a still image.

overview.h2: Choose the first asset your product needs
overview.d: Start with the asset that answers the next shopper question: a clear listing photo, a setting that adds context, or a short clip that shows movement. Use one product photo to make and compare several options, then place each result where it helps shoppers understand the item. Review the generated details against the product you sell, and add current pricing, offers, and final text in your editor.
